question: A research team keeps adding reports to a project's knowledge base and wants to know what happens as that knowledge grows past what fits in a single conversation. What should they expect?
options: A) Claude moves automatically to a retrieval mode that can draw on up to ten times more project content.
B) Someone with edit rights has to switch retrieval on in the project's settings before it can take effect.
C) Claude keeps only the documents added most recently and quietly disregards the older uploads.
D) The knowledge base has to be split across two projects by hand once it passes the limit.
correct_answers: A) Claude moves automatically to a retrieval mode that can draw on up to ten times more project content.
explanations: Correct. As project knowledge approaches the limit, Claude switches to retrieval automatically and can then hold up to ten times more content, reverting if the knowledge later drops back.
Retrieval for projects is automatic; there is no setting for a member to turn it on or off.
Older documents are not silently dropped; retrieval is what lets the larger knowledge base work.
Splitting by hand is unnecessary, because the switch to retrieval happens without any action.
